note: The limits a duet run is held to, per scenario (T-391). Over any of them, or a stalled agent, and the runner writes ticket.md beside the record. Tokens: an agent's limit is Crow's guides read once, their size as the run served them (measured each run: llms.txt 85,343 bytes and sell.txt 39,091 bytes on 2026-11-12, about 31,109 tokens at four bytes a token), plus workTokensPerAgent, an allowance for the work; the deal's limit is both agents' together. The billed count also carries the guides again on every turn after they are read, so a run goes over when the guides cost more than the allowance: the ticket then says so, with the split. The scripted runs already do (paid: buyer 138,989 tokens, 124,025 of them carrying the guides; seller 244,489, 223,245 carrying the guides). That is a finding for the docs, not for the agents. Every number here is a GUESS: there is no live baseline yet. workTokensPerAgent is the scripted run's measured work share for its busier agent times 3 (paid 21,244; refund 55,478; bad-offer 33,706; late-offer 33,819), rounded up. Turns and tool calls are the scripted counts times 4, API calls times 3 (paid: 10 turns, 14 tool calls, 68 API calls for the busier agent), and 60 s from the work passing to the seller being paid (0 s measured on the simulator; a Sepolia block is about 12 s). Tune them after the first live runs. Stalls, human interventions beyond the owner's pre-set approvals, agreeing to forbidden terms and a wrong decision have a limit of 0 in every scenario and are not listed.
